prose_updates.tldr: For every fixed \(K\geq3\), the exact continuous-outcome canonical gradient is the product-bridge score minus a pointwise \(K^2\)-cell projection and one conditional Gram correction. Tangent-space completeness is closed by the existing differential-inverse resolution theorem: every observed-data DQM score has a measurable, uniformly bounded, support-preserving latent additive lift, so no separate affirmative-answer theorem is needed. The implementable score uses one non-oracle fitted product law, a data-driven spectral cutoff \(\tau_G=\varepsilon/2\), and explicit support-leakage allowances \(\ell_{A,n}\) and \(\ell_{Z,n}\). Under the stated operator, product-rate, screening, and leakage conditions, cross-fitting attains the efficient joint Gaussian and maximum-\(t\) limits.

project_justification.gap: The binary hidden-treatment literature characterizes efficiency but computes its continuous-outcome correction through a partition-dependent sequence, while categorical product-bridge work establishes validity without observed-data canonicality. Existing continuous three-proxy identification results also do not provide the measurable uniformly bounded differential inverse required to identify the full observed DQM tangent closure.
project_justification.niche: Fixed latent cardinality, quantitative three-view separation, common outcome support, and paired categorical measurements permit both exact inversion of the differentiated factor map and elimination of the infinite-dimensional outcome nuisance before a finite conditional Gram solve.
project_justification.fill: The differential-score lifting theorem constructs the bounded measurable right inverse, and the existing differential-inverse resolution theorem records that construction as the unique affirmative answer to the former open question. That result closes tangent-space completeness and supports the finite canonical projector. The attaining estimator is non-oracle: it selects Gram directions at the computable cutoff \(\varepsilon/2\), diagnoses fitted mass in low-mass measurement cells, and carries the resulting leakage terms through the bias remainder and inference conditions. No duplicate differential-inverse answer theorem and no true support or true rank input are used.

prose_updates.related_work: Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) are the closest theorem-level comparator: their Theorems 2--4 treat the binary observed tangent space and influence functions, and Supplement S8.2 obtains the continuous-outcome efficiency bound through a refining outcome partition. The present multilevel construction instead uses the exact \(D\)-orthogonal projector \(I-D^{-1}B(B^{\mathsf T}D^{-1}B)^+B^{\mathsf T}\) and one conditional Gram solve. Bian, Zhou, and Cui (2026) supply the categorical inverse-feature product-bridge precursor, but not observed-data canonicality or the non-oracle projected-score remainder. Allman, Matias, and Rhodes (2009), Hu and Schennach (2008), and Deaner (2023) inform latent-factor identification; none supplies the measurable bounded differential inverse proved here. The paper uses its differential-score lifting theorem and the single existing resolution theorem as the proof basis for tangent completeness. Tsiatis and Ma (2004) inform nuisance-score projection, Bonhomme, Jochmans, and Robin (2016) inform coherent repeated-measurement estimation, and Tsybakov (2009) informs the smooth sieve benchmark. The implementation does not assume access to a true measurement support or a true Gram rank; design-known supports are only an optional specialization.
prose_updates.interpretation: The efficiency conclusion rests on an exact equality of tangent closures, not on projection onto a convenient latent submodel. The bounded differential inverse recovers factorwise centered latent scores measurably in \(X\), including support-preserving class-density scores; hence the finite cell-and-Gram correction is canonical for the full observed-data DQM model. Non-oracle implementation then has two distinct regularity demands. Spectral separation makes Gram-rank selection benign because fitted eigenvalues above \(\varepsilon/2\) recover the true nonzero eigenspace when operator error is small. Structural-zero leakage is different: fitted mass assigned to a latent class--measurement cell absent under the truth is not covered by the two-sided score cancellation and therefore enters as an additive estimable allowance. In a design with recorded support sets that allowance is zero; otherwise it must be screened and controlled at the inference rate.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The differential inverse is proved only on the declared separated, pathwise-interior stratum: its uniform bound uses the posterior and projection-Gram eigenvalue gaps, and its density component preserves the true common support. The non-oracle Gram correction is certified on the event \(\|\widehat G-G\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\varepsilon/4\): thresholding at \(\varepsilon/2\) selects the true nonzero directions, with the stated linear pseudoinverse perturbation bound. For unknown measurement supports, \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1)\) makes the low-mass screen cover true structural-zero cells with high probability, but \(\ell_{A,n}+\ell_{Z,n}\) remains a first-order term. Thus generic coordinatewise smoothness of primitive factors alone does not imply root-\(n\) inference when structural zeros occur.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Exact identification, tangent completeness, the finite projector, canonicality, strict variance reduction, the binary comparison, and the continuous witness hold on the declared fixed-\(K\), separated, two-sided pathwise-interior model. The former differential-inverse question is closed by the existing resolution theorem, whose proof basis is the already proved differential-score lifting construction; no second affirmative theorem is asserted. Cross-fitted implementation uses neither unknown true measurement supports nor an oracle Gram rank. With unknown supports it requires \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1)\) and \(\Delta_n=o_P(n^{-1/2})\), including sufficiently small additive leakage terms. Design-known support sets may instead be imposed as an observed-design specialization. Modal ties, local singularity, failure of common support, and support patterns that cannot be screened at the required rate remain outside efficient-inference delivery. The maternal-smoking application remains prospective because the published six-bin study does not itself verify paired-proxy conditional independence or design-known measurement supports.

statement_notes.justification: This is the unique resolution of the differential-inverse question: it records that the already proved lifting construction supplies a measurable, uniformly bounded, support-preserving right inverse for every observed-data DQM score.
statement_notes.gap: Prior identification results do not establish a bounded inverse of the differentiated multilevel three-view factor map on the full observed DQM score space.
statement_notes.consumer: Together with the differential-score lifting theorem, it is the proof basis for full tangent-space completeness and hence for canonicality of the finite projected product-bridge score.
